T2:3:0.text: Coming home from the plot worse than she went

T2:5:0.text: Too pressed by the jungle to look at the children

T2:7:0.text: Feeling watched and found wanting by the other plot holders

T2:9:0.text: Shamed to tears by the committee letter

T2:11:0.text: A blameless record here spoiled by a letter about vegetables

T2:11:1.text: Not one to give hard things back

T2:13:0.text: Hiding from the other plot holders since the letter

T2:15:0.text: Sunflowers taller than her son: exactly what she wanted

T2:19:0.text: Lonely in seeing the mess so the children need not

T2:21:0.text: Even her free hour spent on guilt

T2:23:0.text: Kept on only for her son, herself the help

T2:27:0.text: Outdone in three weeks by her mother

T2:29:0.text: A minute in her buni's garden, then a guest on her own plot

T2:31:0.text: Praised for her mother's work: grateful and small

T2:33:0.text: Struck that her mother remade here the garden she chose to leave

T2:35:0.text: Grateful for a kitchen smelling of home

T2:37:0.text: The good tired gone: the plot one more grey thing

T2:39:0.text: Behind with everything, and most visibly at the plot

T2:41:0.text: Woken from a dream of the plot, not sure she likes it

groups.label: A guest in her mother's half, “grateful and small”
groups.description: Her mother clearing in three weeks what she could not in three months, a garden she chose to leave, and Nell grateful and small

groups.label: Shamed by a letter, and hiding from the plot holders
groups.description: Her name written down, a blameless record spoiled over vegetables, and early mornings at the far fence

groups.label: Awake to being behind, and not one to give it back
groups.description: Seeing only what is undone, racing the weeds, the good tired gone, and still not one to give things back

groups.label: The help on her son's plot
groups.description: Kept on for him, his sunflowers exactly what she wanted, the mess hers alone to see, and her own deckchair never opened

quoted.T2:29:0: "it looked like my buni's garden. … And for one minute I was so happy. Like I opened a door and the village was there. And then the next minute I felt like a visitor. … I was standing on my own plot like a guest."
quoted.T2:9:0: "I read it in the car, outside the nursery, and I cried. … Like somebody walked past my plot with a clipboard and wrote my name down."
quoted.T2:39:0: "Behind is my whole body. I wake up already behind. … And instead it's the place where I'm most behind of all, where you can see how behind I am, with your eyes, in weeds."
quoted.T2:23:0: "And I cannot say to him we're not going any more. I cannot do this. So I suppose it's his now, really. The plot is his and I am the help."
